definition: Interest that is added to an investment and then earns interest itself, so at a rate of $r$ per cent the value is multiplied by $1 + \frac{r}{100}$ each period.
A loss of value over time; at a rate of $r$ per cent a year the value is multiplied by $1 - \frac{r}{100}$ each year.
The yearly interest rate a bank quotes before compounding is taken into account; compounded $k$ times a year, each period earns $\frac{r}{k}$ per cent.
The amount invested or owed at the start, written $PV$.
The value of an investment or item at a later time, written $FV$.
The general rise in prices over time, given as a percentage per year.
What a future amount of money is worth in today's prices, after allowing for inflation.
